key_insight: This paper argues that AI should be deliberately aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) rather than optimized only for technical performance or commercial value. It reframes AI development around societal impact, helping researchers and developers prioritize applications that support sustainability, equity, and human well-being.
problem_solved: AI progress is often disconnected from the world’s most urgent sustainability challenges, leading to misaligned incentives and uneven social benefit. The paper addresses how to steer AI research, deployment, and evaluation toward measurable contributions to the SDGs.
method: Proposes a sustainability-oriented framing for AI design and deployment, linking AI capabilities to SDG targets.
Encourages evaluation beyond accuracy and efficiency to include social, environmental, and developmental outcomes.
Highlights alignment strategies that help map AI solutions to high-priority real-world problems.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer roadmap for building systems that are not just technically strong but also socially responsible and policy-relevant. It can influence research agendas, benchmarking practices, and product decisions toward broader positive impact.
visual_elements: SDG wheel or grid showing AI applications mapped to specific SDG goals
Before/after pipeline comparing traditional AI optimization vs SDG-aligned AI
Impact flow diagram from AI model outputs to societal/environmental outcomes
Icon set representing sustainability themes such as climate, health, education, and equity
paper_title: Realigning AI technology towards the Sustainable Development Goals
paper_authors: Rundong Feng, Ziming Li, Bojie Fu, Huadong Guo, Jianguo Liu
